document_summary: Part 1 of 3 of Newark, NJ Code Chapter 19:2 (Rent Control Regulations; Rent Control Board), covering the policy statement, definitions, exemptions, annual CPI-based rent increase cap, surcharges, hardship increases and registration provisions. | Part 2 of 3 of Newark, NJ Code ch. 19:2 (Rent Control), covering registration, Rent Control Board powers, rent decreases, hearings, utilities surcharge, new-construction and rehabilitation exemptions, the 25% annual limit, fees and inspections. | Part 3 of Newark, NJ Code ch. 19:2 (added 5-20-2026) covering rental-unit inspections, certificates of habitability, occupancy limits and revocation, which are housing-code and registration provisions outside the six rule categories.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: annual CPI-based rent increase cap
rules.requirement: At lease expiration (or termination of a periodic tenancy), a landlord may not request or receive an increase greater than the CPI-U change measured from 15 months to 3 months before the month of the proposed increase, and never more than 4%. Written notice of at least 30 days must go to the tenant and the Rent Regulation Officer, and no increase is allowed unless the dwelling is in substantial compliance and the landlord has registered.
rules.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings as defined in § 19:2-2 are subject to rent control (§ 19:2-2.1). The cap applies to any 12-month period regardless of tenant turnover, ownership change or vacancy (§ 19:2-3.2).
rules.exemptions: Public housing; hotel/motel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings per §§ 19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2 (details not in this part); certain federal/state rehabilitated Section 8 units (rent capped at HUD fair market rent); units under a preemptive government rent-regulation contract.
rules.interaction: Municipal rent control; the tenant-facing cap is separate from tax, major new improvement and hardship surcharges, which the Rent Control Board may grant. The chapter is not shown to conflict with state law in this document.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Section history shows original Ord. 6 PSF-A(S) of 9-5-2017, amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I; the text does not say which amendment set the 4% ceiling, so the 2024 date is the latest amendment. Newer Ord. 6PSF-C (06-17-2026) amends only §§ 19:2-27 and 19:2-32, not this section. Detailed exemptions in §§ 19:2-18.x are in a later part of the document.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control - limitation on increases (25% ceiling) and exemptions
rules.requirement: The Rent Control Board may not grant any tenant rent increases exceeding 25% in any one year, counting regular, major-improvement and hardship increases within the prior 12 months. Other ceilings apply to utilities surcharges and vacant-unit rehabilitation increases.
rules.key_value: Board may not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year (regular CPI-based annual increase is in § 19:2-3, not in this part)
rules.coverage_conditions: Dwellings subject to Newark's rent control chapter; rents controlled at the level received as of the chapter's first adoption on September 4, 1985, with the chapter continuing in force from October 19, 1988.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt for the lesser of the initial-mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion (30 years if no mortgage). Vacant properties vacant 18 months and rehabilitated at over 50% of fair market value are exempt for five years. Substantially rehabilitated dwellings may set an unrestricted initial rent. Vacant-unit rehabilitation (spending at least 12 months of rent) allows a maximum 10% increase, once per 12 months. Utilities surcharge is capped at 15% of the monthly rent roll for 30 or fewer units, 5% for 31-200 units and 3% for over 200 units.
rules.quoted_span: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.
rules.extraction_notes: The tenant-facing annual allowable increase (§ 19:2-3) is in another part of the chapter and is not in this capture. No effective date is stated for § 19:2-22 (amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. 6PSF-I per history note); the later 5-20-2026 amendments touch other sections (vacant properties, substantial rehabilitation, fees, inspections), so effective_date is null.

rules.title: Retaliatory eviction prohibition (Newark rent control)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce rights under the rent control chapter.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants asserting rights under Newark's rent control chapter.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
rules.out_of_scope_reason: Anti-retaliation provision, excluded from the just-cause category by scope rules.
rules.extraction_notes: Logged only; the section does not limit the grounds for eviction or non-renewal generally.
